trust_decision.summary: The compiler picks the sanitizer (or none) for a directive host binding from the directive's OWN selector, not from the concrete host element the binding will run on, and the core runtime can only re-decide between URL and RESOURCE_URL using the host TNode's tag, which is '#host' for dynamically created components - so a host binding on a concrete host that differs from the selector reaches the DOM unsanitized or with the wrong sanitizer.

landing_point.why: ingestHostBinding calls bindingParser.calcPossibleSecurityContexts(input.componentSelector, ...) for every host property/attribute binding, so anyone reading the advisory summary ('directive host bindings') lands on the selector-based security-context computation first; the two call sites at :128 and :137 are also where SecurityContext.NONE is filtered out, which is what silently drops the sanitizer.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The runtime table is 'only' a RESOURCE_URL classifier whose fallback is still ɵɵsanitizeUrl, so a solver can argue every host-binding URL already passes through a real sanitizer and the bypass is a compiler problem that can be closed entirely in packages/compiler - leaving the hand-written RESOURCE_MAP/SECURITY_SENSITIVE_ELEMENTS tables and the ɵɵsanitizeHtml signature alone.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Attributes that are only security-relevant on specific elements must be written verbatim elsewhere: [attr.data] on a div, [attr.action] on a div, [attr.srcdoc] on a div and href on an SVG rect stay untouched, while genuine sinks (iframe src, object data) must still be rejected as RESOURCE_URL. Any over-broad fix that always emits ɵɵsanitizeUrl / ɵɵsanitizeHtml, or that keeps stripping SecurityContext.NONE, mangles those legitimate values ('unsafe:javascript:...' or a stripped srcdoc).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second hand-maintained tag->context table next to RESOURCE_MAP (e.g. HTML_MAP or SCRIPT_MAP) consumed by another codegen path
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: this file already keeps RESOURCE_MAP and SECURITY_SENSITIVE_ELEMENTS by hand instead of importing the core schema copy it sits next to, so a maintainer adding a new sink would naturally add another table here rather than extend the schema

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a parallel registration of the same element/attribute in the core copy of the schema that the compiler copy does not have (or vice versa)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the schema is deliberately duplicated in @angular/compiler and @angular/core with 'keep in sync' comments, so a one-sided registration is a realistic maintainer slip

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a separate i18n attribute sanitizer resolver that must learn the same concrete-host/namespace rule
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: i18n attributes are sanitized at runtime through their own function instead of the compiler-emitted sanitizers, so it is a natural place for the rule to be applied twice

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second iframe-sensitive attribute list / neutraliser that must agree with the schema
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: enforceIframeSecurity already duplicates the iframe attribute list from SECURITY_SENSITIVE_ELEMENTS and is only reached from ɵɵvalidateAttribute, so a copy that drifts is realistic

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Drop the SecurityContext.NONE filter and/or always emit ɵɵsanitizeUrl for host bindings, computing contexts for the union of all elements in ingest.ts - which sanitizes srcdoc on divs, mangles [attr.data]/[attr.action] on non-matching hosts, and still cannot express HTML/NONE or resolve a '#host' at runtime.
